notes: The validator covers pure-computation functions (PKCS7, AES key schedule, RSA, LFSR, hash, side-channel stats) with no matching MCP tool surface. The only MCP tool for this crate is crypto_xor_decode (file+VA based). Three XOR-decode tests were run: (1) single-byte explicit key -> PASS, (2) auto-detect on 13-byte sample chose key 0x40 instead of 0x42 (both yield fully-printable output, printable-ratio heuristic is ambiguous on short input) -> MISMATCH, (3) multi-byte 2-byte key 'DEAD' 46 bytes -> PASS. The pure-computation validator functions (sha1, expand_aes128, berlekamp_massey, wiener_attack, pearson_correlation, etc.) have no corresponding MCP tool and cannot be compared via JSON-RPC.

test_cases.reason: Auto-detect printable-ratio heuristic is ambiguous on 13-byte samples: key 0x40 yields 100% printable output just like key 0x42. Both are technically valid; heuristic picks first maximum. Not a correctness bug — a fundamental limitation of single-metric brute-force on short input.
